message.content:
Repo: H:\Kasirku (Next.js 16 App Router POS/accounting SaaS, "Kasirku"). I'm building a new cashier-facing page: a focused "Printer Dapur & Bar" view reachable from the POS screen's Menu panel, showing the list of configured kitchen printers with a "Tes Cetak" (test print) button per printer — view + test only, no add/edit/delete (that stays in the existing Settings page).

I need facts about the current code, not recommendations:

1. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx` — find the "☰ Menu" panel (added in an earlier session) that links to Riwayat Transaksi/Laporan/Riwayat Shift. Show me the exact JSX for that panel/menu list (component structure, how links are rendered, businessId access pattern, whether it's a Sheet/Drawer/Dialog component) so I can add one more entry to it.

2. `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx` — show the exact printer-list rendering block (the `printers.map(...)` section, roughly lines 190-215) including what columns/fields are shown (name, connection_type, address, device_label, categories) — I need to replicate similar display logic in the new page.

3. `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts` — show the full current file (post a recent edit adding `connectionType` to `KitchenPrintJobPayload` and `buildKitchenPrintJobs`). Also show `src/lib/escpos.ts`'s full content (the `buildKitchenTicket` function) so I know what ticket-building primitives exist for constructing a small standalone "test print" ticket for ONE specific printer (not routed by category/items).

4. `src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts` — show its full current content (the `dispatchPrintJobs`/`dispatchOne` functions) so I know the exact shape of `KitchenPrintJobPayload` a caller needs to construct, and confirm it's already a "use client" file I can import directly into a new client component.

5. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/actions.ts` — show the imports/exports list only (just names, not full bodies) so I know what's already there (e.g., `logKitchenPrintFailures`) and don't duplicate.

6. Check whether there's an existing pattern in this codebase for a route nested under `pos/` (e.g. `pos/check-in/page.tsx` — check if that folder exists and how its page.tsx is structured: Server Component fetching data + rendering, or something else) so the new printer page can follow the same layout/auth convention (how does it get the cashier session / businessId, does it use the same shell/header as other POS subpages).

Report factual code excerpts with file:line references — I'll design the new page myself from this.

## Findings ### 1. `☰ Menu` panel — `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx` It's a plain custom modal/sheet (no Sheet/Drawer/Dialog library component — same hand-rolled "bottom sheet on mobile, centered dialog on desktop" pattern used for all the other overlays in this file: Bon, Order inbox, etc.). It's controlled by local `useState`, not a portal/primitive component. State declaration (line 137): ```tsx const [posMenuOpen, setPosMenuOpen] = useState(false); ``` Trigger button (lines 915-920, in the top toolbar next to Bon/Order/OfflineStatus): ```tsx ``` Full panel JSX (lines 1466-1517): ```tsx {/* Open bills */} {posMenuOpen && (
setPosMenuOpen(false)} />

☰ Menu

setPosMenuOpen(false)} className="flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 px-3.5 py-3 text-sm font-medium text-zinc-700 transition-colors hover:bg-zinc-50" > 🧾 Riwayat Transaksi setPosMenuOpen(false)} className="flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 px-3.5 py-3 text-sm font-medium text-zinc-700 transition-colors hover:bg-zinc-50" > 📊 Laporan setPosMenuOpen(false)} className="flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 px-3.5 py-3 text-sm font-medium text-zinc-700 transition-colors hover:bg-zinc-50" > 🕒 Riwayat Shift

Dibuka di tab baru — keranjang belanja kamu tidak hilang.

)} ``` Notes: - Entries are plain `` (not `next/link`) with `target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"` — these routes open in a new tab so the cart state in `PosScreen` survives. The stray `{/* Open bills */}` comment above line 1466 is a leftover/misplaced comment (belongs to the block below it), not attached to this menu. - `businessId` comes straight from the component's props (destructured at line 88-116; it's a plain string prop, no context/hook). - All comparable overlays (`billsOpen`, `inboxOpen`, `cashMoveOpen`, etc.) follow the same pattern: a backdrop `div` with `onClick` to close, plus a `relative` sheet `div`. If your new "Printer Dapur & Bar" entry navigates to a full page rather than opening inline, it should be another `` line inside this same `
` block; if you want it as an in-place panel instead, you'd add a new `useState` boolean and a new conditional block styled like this one. ### 2. Printer list rendering — `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx:200-219` ```tsx {printers.length > 0 ? ( printers.map((p) => (

{p.name}

{p.connection_type === "lan" ? "🌐 LAN/Wi-Fi" : "📶 Bluetooth"} {p.address ? ` · ${p.connection_type === "bluetooth" ? (p.device_label ?? p.address) : p.address}` : ""}

{p.categories.length > 0 && (

Kategori: {p.categories.join(", ")}

)}
)) ) : (

Belum ada printer dapur/bar. Order akan tetap dicetak di kasir saja.

)} ``` Fields shown: `name` (bold), `connection_type` (emoji-labeled "🌐 LAN/Wi-Fi" or "📶 Bluetooth"), `address`/`device_label` (Bluetooth shows `device_label ?? address`; LAN shows `address` directly), `categories` (joined list, only rendered if non-empty). The query that produces this data (lines 96-102): ```tsx const { data: printerRows } = await supabase .from("kitchen_printers") .select("id, name, categories, connection_type, address, device_label") .eq("business_id", businessId) .order("name", { ascending: true }); printers = printerRows ?? []; ``` Row type (lines 86-93): `{ id: string; name: string; categories: string[]; connection_type: string; address: string | null; device_label: string | null }`. ### 3. `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts` (full, 69 lines) and `src/lib/escpos.ts` (full, 57 lines) Both shown in full above. Key exports: - `KitchenPrintJobPayload` (kitchen-print.ts:18-23): `{ printerName: string; address: string; connectionType: "lan" | "bluetooth"; bytesBase64: string }`. - `buildKitchenPrintJobs(supabase, businessId, job)` — fans a `KitchenPrintJob` (`{ source, label, items }`) out to every printer whose `categories` match (or all printers if `categories` is empty), building one ticket buffer per printer via `buildKitchenTicket`. - `buildKitchenTicket(input: KitchenTicketInput): Buffer` (escpos.ts:25-56) — the primitive you'd reuse for a standalone test ticket. `KitchenTicketInput = { station: string; source: string; label: string; items: KitchenTicketItem[] }`, `KitchenTicketItem = { name: string; qty: number; note?: string | null }`. It ESC/POS-inits, centers+enlarges `station`, prints `"{source} - {label}"` + a localized timestamp + a dashed rule, then bold `qty x name` (+ optional note) per item, feeds, and partial-cuts. For a one-off "Tes Cetak" ticket for a single printer you already have `name`/`address`/`connection_type` for (no DB lookup needed, no category routing), you can call `buildKitchenTicket({ station: printer.name, source: "Tes Cetak", label: "...", items: [...] })` directly and base64-encode the returned `Buffer`, then hand it to `dispatchPrintJobs` as a single-element `KitchenPrintJobPayload[]` — you don't need `buildKitchenPrintJobs` at all since that function's whole job is category-based multi-printer routing, which a single-printer test print doesn't need. ### 4. `src/lib/dispatch-print-jobs.ts` (full, 55 lines, shown above) - Line 1: `"use client";` — confirmed already a client file, importable directly into a new client component. - `dispatchPrintJobs(businessId: string, jobs: KitchenPrintJobPayload[]): Promise` — fire-and-forget; on any failed job it calls the server action `logKitchenPrintFailures(businessId, [{printer, error}])` from `pos/actions.ts` (swallowing its own errors with `.catch(() => {})`). - `dispatchOne(job: KitchenPrintJobPayload): Promise` — branches on `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()`: native → `KitchenPrinter.printLan`/`printBluetooth` (Capacitor plugin), web → `printViaAgent(job.address, job.bytesBase64)` for `"lan"` and returns `{ ok: false, reason: "printer_unreachable", error: "unsupported_on_web" }` for `"bluetooth"` on plain browsers. - Caller only needs to construct `KitchenPrintJobPayload = { printerName, address, connectionType, bytesBase64 }` and call `dispatchPrintJobs(businessId, [payload])`. ### 5. `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/actions.ts` — imports/exports only Imports: ```ts import { revalidatePath } from "next/cache"; import { createClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server"; import { setCashierSession, clearCashierSession } from "@/lib/cashier-session"; import { logActivity } from "@/lib/activity-log"; import { buildKitchenPrintJobs, type KitchenPrintJobPayload } from "@/lib/kitchen-print"; ``` Exports (function/type names only): ``` verifyPin switchCashier type DiscountType type CartItemInput type CheckoutResult checkout logKitchenPrintFailures type OpenShiftResult openShift type CloseShiftSummary type CloseShiftResult closeShift type CashMovementResult addShiftCashMovement type OpenBillItemInput type SaveOpenBillResult saveOpenBill deleteOpenBill updateSelfOrderStatus ``` (`buildKitchenPrintJobsForItems` is a local, non-exported helper.) `logKitchenPrintFailures` already exists here and is exactly what `dispatch-print-jobs.ts` imports — no need to duplicate it for the new page's error logging if you want the same failure-logging behavior for test prints. ### 6. `pos/check-in/` nested-route pattern `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/check-in/page.tsx` (full, 61 lines, shown above) exists and is a Server Component: - Fetches `business` (`id, name`) by `businessId`, `notFound()` if missing. - Calls `getCashierSession(businessId)` from `@/lib/cashier-session`. If no session → renders `` (reusing the *parent* `pos/pin-screen.tsx` via `../pin-screen`) to force PIN entry first — this is the auth gate, same one `pos/page.tsx` uses. - If session exists → fetches page-specific data (here, `ticket_categories`) and renders a local client component, `CheckInScreen` (`./check-in-screen`), passing `businessId`, `businessName`, `cashierId`, `cashierName` (from `session`), plus fetched data as props. - No shared "shell"/header wrapper is imported in this file — layout chrome comes from `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/layout.tsx` (the parent POS layout), and `CheckInScreen` itself builds its own screen top-to-bottom (same as `PosScreen` does), it isn't wrapped in a shared header component here. So the convention for a new `pos/printer-dapur/page.tsx` (or similar) would be: Server Component → fetch `business`, `notFound()` guard → `getCashierSession(businessId)` → if absent render `` (from `../pin-screen`), else fetch `kitchen_printers` rows (same select as settings page) and render a new client `*-screen.tsx` component with `businessId`, `businessName`, `cashierId`, `cashierName`, and `printers` as props, inheriting chrome from `pos/layout.tsx`.
